chunks: Samaʿah ibn Mihrān asked him about a man who died and had no one with him except women, so he said:
"A woman who is his mahram should wash him, and the women should pour water over him, and she should not remove his garment.
If it is a woman who has died among men, and there is no woman with them and no mahram for her, then she should be buried as she is in her clothes.
And if a mahram of hers is with her, he should wash her from over her clothes."

key_terms.النِّسَاءُ: the women present with the deceased man
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: the water used for washing the deceased
key_terms.ثَوْبَهُ: his garment, which is not to be removed during the washing
key_terms.ثِيَابِهَا: her clothes, over which washing is to be done or in which she is to be buried
key_terms.ذَاتُ مَحْرَمٍ: a woman who is within the prohibited degrees of marriage to him, permitting limited handling in this context
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a male mahram relative of the deceased woman

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a deceased man or woman has only non-matching attendants present for ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about washing the deceased when only members of the opposite sex are present. It distinguishes between the presence or absence of a mahram and instructs that modesty be preserved by washing over clothing or, in some cases, proceeding to burial in the clothes as they are.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.431 - Sama’a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a man who dies and is only accompanied by women.
Imam (as) replied: "A woman who is his mahram (close relative) should wash him, and the other women should pour water over him without removing his clothes.
If it is a woman who dies among men, with no women or mahram present, She should be buried as She is in her clothing.
If a mahram is present, he may wash her from over her clothes."
